references.text: Describes the departure from Horeb (Sinai) and the journey through the wilderness, the same event mentioned in Deuteronomy.
Mentions Kadesh-Barnea as the destination where the spies were sent out, the same place mentioned here.
Refers to Kadesh-Barnea and the events there, including the report of the spies.
Describes the great and terrible wilderness with snakes and scorpions, the same wilderness mentioned here.
Horeb is mentioned as God's mountain, the starting point for the journey noted in this verse.
Mentions Hazeroth and the wilderness of Paran as part of the route toward Kadesh.
Describes the wilderness as a desolate, howling wasteland—the same terrible wilderness mentioned here.
Refers to Moses leading the people through the wilderness, the same event described here.
The book of Hebrews refers to the generation that left Egypt and wandered in the wilderness, warning against the same kind of unbelief.
Stephen speaks about Moses who led the people out and performed wonders in the wilderness for forty years.
